QuestionStmt.S: If the sum of the squares of the distance of the point $P(x, y, z)$ from the coordinate axes is 242, then the distance of the point $P$ from the origin is ______ units.

Solution.S:
Distance of $P(x,y,z)$ from x-axis = $\sqrt{y^2+z^2}$, from y-axis = $\sqrt{x^2+z^2}$, from z-axis = $\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$.

Sum of squares: $(y^2+z^2) + (x^2+z^2) + (x^2+y^2) = 2(x^2+y^2+z^2) = 242$.

Thus $x^2+y^2+z^2 = 121$.

Distance from origin = $\sqrt{x^2+y^2+z^2} = \sqrt{121} = 11$.

Hence correct option is B: 11.
